1	# Augment Poll (C2) — the poller contract
2	
3	This ref pins the poll surface and timing for the in-session Monitor. The poll **script**
4	(`scripts/poll-augment-review.sh`) performs a single `gh`/`gh api` poll and emits one JSON line; the
5	**FSM** (`superclaude.pr_submit`) does the backoff arithmetic. This split keeps `gh` out of the
6	deterministic core (NFR-6) — the script touches `gh`, the core decides.
7	
8	> Every `gh`/`gh api` call below pins the RESOLVED `--repo <owner/repo>` (origin's `nameWithOwner`,
9	> FR-1.3 / AC-7). A bare `gh` without `--repo` is a defect (T-104 greps for it).
10	
11	## Poll surfaces (FR-2.1)
12	
13	Primary, the exact `--json` field set from the spec:
14	
15	```bash
16	gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json number,url,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName,reviews,comments
17	```
18	
19	- `headRefOid` = the head SHA (used by INV-001 `sha_attributed_to_our_push` and the inline-reply
20	  `commit_id`).
21	- `reviews` = `{author{login}, authorAssociation, state, body, submittedAt, url}`.
22	- `comments` = PR conversation comments (NOT inline review comments).
23	
24	REST surfaces (inline-comment ids / `in_reply_to_id` are not on `gh pr view`, so REST is required):
25	
26	```bash
27	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/reviews
28	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/comments
29	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/commits/<headSHA>/check-runs   # only if the probe shows emission_shape==check_run
30	```
31	
32	Classification is pure against the probe-locked `DetectionContract` (`detection-contract.md`): key on
33	`augment_bot_login`; four states no-review / clean / findings / **declined** (T-201/202/203 + FR-9.1).
34	The V1.1 `declined` state fires when an Augment-authored comment matches BOTH probe-locked decline
35	regexes (`decline_phrase_regex` "abnormally large" AND `decline_retrigger_regex` "comment
36	augment/auggie/augmentcode review"), watermark-aware (a stale pre-watermark decline is ignored, EC-23).
37	The decline ARITHMETIC (the both-regex AND, the watermark comparison, the strict-once routing) stays in
38	the deterministic core; only the decline raw-surfacing comes from this poll script — the same
39	script-polls / FSM-decides seam as the other states. The decline is posted by the App as a **PR
40	conversation comment** (the `gh pr view --json comments` surface, equivalently `issues/<N>/comments` —
41	the same surface `retrigger-review.sh` posts to), NOT as an inline review comment. The poll script
42	therefore **merges** the conversation comments (`.comments` from `gh pr view`) with the inline review
43	comments (`pulls/<N>/comments`) into the emitted `comments` array, so the classifier sees the decline;
44	surfacing only the inline comments would make `declined` unreachable in production. (The classifier's
45	finding-comment rule requires `path`+`line`, so the path-less conversation comments are never miscounted
46	as findings.)
47	
48	## Interval, timeout, backoff (FR-2.3 / FR-2.5 / NFR-2)
49	
50	- **Interval ≥ 30s.** A value below 30 is **rejected, not rounded** ("minimum is 30 seconds", T-111).
51	- **Timeout default 600s** (~10 min), configurable; **wall-clock since entering wait** (T-221/T-222).
52	- **Exponential backoff on 403 / 429 / secondary-limit:** `30 → 60 → 120 → … → cap 300s`, resetting
53	  on a successful poll (T-231). The backoff **counts toward the wall-clock timeout**.
54	
55	## Division of labour (the NFR-6 seam)
56	
57	- The **poll script** does ONE `gh`/`gh api` poll and returns a status line (`polling` / `clean` /
58	  `findings`, plus the raw payload for classification). It performs no arithmetic and holds no state.
59	- The **FSM** owns the backoff arithmetic (which interval to use next, whether the cap or the timeout
60	  is reached) and the state transitions. This keeps the `gh` I/O isolated to the script and the
61	  deterministic decisions in `superclaude.pr_submit` (NFR-6). The ref explicitly assigns the backoff
62	  arithmetic to the FSM, never the script.
63

1	---
2	name: pr-submit
3	description: "Open a PR on the fork and arm an in-session PR-review auto-remediation monitor — poll for the Augment review, re-grade + verify findings, dispatch verified ones to /sc:troubleshoot, then (at higher --monitor ordinals) fix, validate, push, reply, and resolve under a capped monotonic round counter."
4	category: quality
5	complexity: advanced
6	mcp-servers: [sequential, serena, auggie]
7	personas: [analyzer, architect, security, qa, devops]
8	argument-hint: "--monitor {0,1,2,3} [--max-rounds N≤5] [--poll-interval ≥30] [--timeout 600] [--base <branch>] [--head <branch>] [--title ...] [--body ...] [--output-dir <dir>] [--resume <run-log.jsonl>]"
9	version: "1.0"
10	---
11	
12	# /sc:pr-submit - PR Review Auto-Remediation Monitor
13	
14	## Triggers
15	
16	Explicit only — three activation paths:
17	
18	1. **Direct:** the user runs `/sc:pr-submit --monitor {0,1,2,3}` to open a PR (and optionally arm the monitor).
19	2. **PR-creation hook:** after a successful `gh pr create`, the `offer-pr-review.sh` hook mentions `sc:pr-submit --monitor` alongside `/sc:auggie-review` (the hook NEVER arms a monitor itself, NEVER implies level-3 without explicit invocation).
20	3. **Programmatic:** another skill invokes the protocol via the Skill tool.
21	
22	## Required Input
23	
24	| Input | Required | Notes |
25	|-------|----------|-------|
26	| `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` | No (default 1) | The autonomy ceiling on a single FSM. Explicit 0 = open PR only (byte-identical to today). |
27	| PR context (`--head`/`--base`/`--title`/`--body`) OR an existing PR number | Yes | To open or attach to the PR. |
28	
29	**STOP** if `--monitor >= 1` and the PR cannot be confirmed on the resolved target repo (origin's `owner/repo`, via `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`), or if `detection-contract.md` is `locked: false` (run the R1 probe first — T-210).
30	
31	## Usage
32	
33	```text
34	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 0 --head feature/x --title "..." --body "..."     # open PR only (zero regression)
35	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 1 --head feature/x                                 # arm + poll + propose (no edits)
36	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 2 --head feature/x                                 # + fix locally, HALT before push
37	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --max-rounds 3 --head feature/x                  # full loop: fix→push→reply→resolve
38	/sc:pr-submit --resume <repo-root>/.dev/pr-monitor/pr-42-.../monitor-run-42.jsonl
39	```
40	
41	## Options
42	
43	| Flag | Default | Description |
44	|------|---------|-------------|
45	| `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` | 1 | Capability ceiling (G-arm/G-edit/G-push gates). |
46	| `--max-rounds N` | 2 | Remediation cycles; hard cap 5 (reject >5). |
47	| `--poll-interval S` | 30 | Poll interval; minimum 30 seconds (reject <30). |
48	| `--timeout S` | 600 | Review-wait wall-clock timeout (~10 min). |
49	| `--base <branch>` | repo default branch | PR base branch; defaults to the repo's actual default (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`), overridable here. |
50	| `--head <branch>` | — | PR head branch. |
51	| `--title` / `--body` | — | PR title / body. |
52	| `--output-dir <dir>` | `.dev/pr-monitor/pr-<N>-<ts>/` | Run-log + artifacts dir. |
53	| `--resume <jsonl>` | — | Reconstruct state from a write-ahead run-log. |
54	
55	## Behavioral Flow
56	
57	This command does ONLY parse + environment-validate + handoff. It parses the flags, verifies the PR target is the resolved origin repo (origin's `owner/repo`, never an upstream parent the host's CLI might default to), and hands off to the protocol skill via the Activation section below. The full behavioral specification — the FSM, the detection contract, severity routing, verify-before-remediate, troubleshoot dispatch, validation gates, the push triad, reply/resolve, and the loop guard — lives in the skill.
58	
59	## Arming (R1 detection probe, T-210)
60	
61	`--monitor 0` always works (it just opens the PR). To arm at `--monitor >= 1`, the detection contract must be locked. The shipped `refs/detection-contract.md` ships `locked: false`, so a fresh clone safely HALTs ("probe first"). To arm on a given repo, run the R1 probe once against a PR the Augment App has reviewed (capture `augment_bot_login`, `emission_shape`, `findings_locus`, etc.), write the gitignored operator-local override `<repo-root>/.dev/pr-monitor/detection-contract.locked.md` with `locked: true`, and the arm path (`DetectionContract.for_arming()`) prefers it (resolved relative to the cwd). The repo-specific bot identity therefore never ships in the distributable skill.
62	
63	## Activation
64	
65	**MANDATORY**: Before executing any protocol steps, invoke:
66	> Skill sc:pr-submit-protocol
67	
68	Pass the following context:
69	
70	- `--monitor` ordinal (0/1/2/3) and `--max-rounds` / `--poll-interval` / `--timeout`.
71	- PR context: `--base` / `--head` / `--title` / `--body`, or the existing PR number.
72	- `--output-dir` and `--resume` if supplied.
73	
74	Do NOT attempt to execute the monitor using only this command file. The deterministic decisions defer to the importable `superclaude.pr_submit` core; the orchestration, Monitor arming, and `gh`/`git` I/O live in the protocol skill.
75	
76	## Boundaries
77	
78	**Will:** open the PR on the resolved origin repo with `--repo <owner/repo>` pinned on every `gh` call (the pin is computed from origin, never bare); arm an in-session monitor at L1+; verify before remediating; respect the ordinal ceiling.
79	
80	**Will Not:** run headless / imply a daemon; push to an upstream parent remote or to the repo's default/protected branch; auto-lock the detection contract; emit `--depth quick --fix`; apply edits at L1 or push/reply at L2.
81	
82	## Related Commands
83	
84	- `/sc:auggie-review` — the sibling PR-review command (offered together by the post-PR-create hook).
85	- `/sc:troubleshoot` — invoked per verified finding for diagnosis.
86

17	
18	`sc:pr-submit` opens a PR on the resolved origin repo (origin's `owner/repo` — never an upstream parent), arms an
19	**in-session** Monitor that polls for the Augment Code review, re-grades each finding's severity
20	through the reused auggie-review rubric, **verifies each finding grounds in real code before

26	**The `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` ordinal is a capability ceiling on a SINGLE finite state machine**
27	(`refs/state-machine.md`), compared at exactly three gates plus one override — NOT four divergent

34	> loses the monitor. Durability comes from the write-ahead JSONL run-log + `--resume`, never from
35	> detachment. This skill cannot survive its own session. Do NOT imply a background daemon.
36	>
37	> **Top-level activation required.** This skill MUST run in the main orchestrating session (so it
38	> has the `Monitor` tool and can `> Skill sc:troubleshoot-protocol`). Do NOT run it inside an

75	## Wave / Phase Structure (refs are LAZY-loaded per wave, never pre-loaded)
76	
77	```text
78	Wave 0: Open PR + verify target   ← (no ref; gh pr create --repo, pre-PR checks)
79	Wave 1: Arm + poll                ← loads refs/detection-contract.md (arm gate) + refs/augment-poll.md
80	Wave 2: Classify + re-grade       ← loads refs/severity-routing.md
81	Wave 3: Verify-before-remediate   ← loads refs/finding-verify.md
82	Wave 4: Diagnose + (L2+) fix      ← loads refs/troubleshoot-dispatch.md
83	Wave 5: Validate                  ← the VAL validator (§10 gate list, below)
84	Wave 6: (L3) push + reply + resolve + re-trigger ← loads refs/thread-reply.md + refs/review-retrigger.md (S5a)
85	Wave 6b: (L3) decline → auggie fallback           ← loads refs/auggie-fallback.md (S5b, strict-once)
86	Wave 7: Loop / terminate          ← loads refs/loop-guard.md
87	```
88	
89	- **Wave 0 (all ordinals):** resolve the target repo once (`REPO="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner)"`, fallback parse `git remote get-url origin`) and the base branch (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name`, overridable via `--base`); open the PR with `gh pr create --repo "$REPO" --base <base> --head <head> --title "..." --body "..."`; confirm `git remote -v` shows origin = `$REPO`; rebase if behind `origin/<base>`; verify the returned URL's `owner/repo` equals `$REPO` (a CLI that defaulted onto an upstream parent is a misroute → HALT). Pass `--repo "$REPO"` to every poll/reply/retrigger script too. At **L0 (`--monitor 0`)** the FSM never leaves `S0_IDLE` — open the PR and return, byte-for-byte identical to today (AC-1). The `offer-pr-review.sh` hook may then mention `sc:pr-submit --monitor`.
90	- **Wave 1 (L1+):** load the locked contract via `superclaude.pr_submit.DetectionContract.for_arming()` — this prefers the **operator-local** locked override (gitignored `.dev/pr-monitor/detection-contract.locked.md`, populated by the R1 probe with this fork's real Augment values) and falls back to the SHIPPED `refs/detection-contract.md` (which stays `locked: false`). **Refuse to arm if no locked contract resolves** (T-210, "probe first"). Initialize the output-dir + run-log + baseline, then call the **`Monitor` tool** with the poll loop wrapping `scripts/poll-augment-review.sh` (interval ≥30s, timeout default 600s); each emitted JSON line advances the FSM. Arm exactly once at L1+ (T-109); never at L0 (T-110).
91	- **Wave 2:** load `refs/severity-routing.md`; call `remap_severity(finding)` from `superclaude.pr_submit` and map the remapped tier to its troubleshoot route (Medium → `--fix`; High/Critical → `--depth deep --fix`; Low/Nit → report-only). NEVER emit `--depth quick --fix`.
92	- **Wave 3:** load `refs/finding-verify.md`; spawn the `evidence-validator` agent (read-only) to confirm each finding's cited file:line exists and the defect reproduces. `unverified` → REPORT_ONLY, consuming NO round.
93	- **Wave 4:** load `refs/troubleshoot-dispatch.md`; for VERIFIED findings only, `> Skill sc:troubleshoot-protocol` for diagnosis. **At L1 (G-edit `ordinal < 2`): PROPOSE "fix these? y/n" and apply NO edits.** At L2+ the skill applies the diagnosed edits ITSELF in the working tree (troubleshoot does NOT auto-apply — `sc:pr-submit` owns edit application in `S3_FIXING`).
94	- **Wave 5:** run the VAL validator (below). **At L2 the ceiling stops here:** after applying the edits in `S3_FIXING` and validating in `S7_VALIDATING`, the FSM HALTs at `S4'_HALT_BEFORE_PUSH` — changes are left in the working tree with NO commit, NO push, NO reply (`S3_FIXING → S7_VALIDATING → S4'_HALT_BEFORE_PUSH`, matching `state-machine.md` §5.2a). Only L3 proceeds to Wave 6.
95	- **Wave 6 (L3 only):** load `refs/thread-reply.md`. The deterministic core DECIDES (evaluates the INV-016 conjunction, records the write-ahead push triad `push_decision` → `push_initiated` (fsynced BEFORE the push) → `push_completed`, keyed on the PRE-push idempotency key `push:<run_id>:<cycle_id>:<pre_push_sha>:<target_branch>`); the SKILL performs the actual `git push origin <target_sha>:<target_branch>` (never an upstream parent remote, never the repo's default/protected branch) ONLY when the conjunction holds, then reply (citing `applied_edits` status — `applied_edits==0` says "no code change applied", never "resolved") and resolve via `scripts/reply-resolve-thread.sh` (reply FIRST, then resolve). **S5a re-trigger (FR-8):** load `refs/review-retrigger.md`; a push does NOT auto-trigger an Augment re-review — AFTER resolve, and ONLY when this cycle applied edits (`applied_edits > 0`), post the re-trigger comment via `scripts/retrigger-review.sh --pr <N>` BEFORE re-entering the S5 poll. The core decides whether/when to re-trigger (`do_retrigger` seam, INV-R1: at most once per push cycle, `rereview_request_count <= max_rounds`); the script does the `gh api` issue-comment POST (NFR-6). On posting the re-trigger, append a **`rereview_requested{cycle_id}`** run-log event (the INV-R1 producer — folded into `rereview_request_count` by `rebuild_state`, and consumed by crash recovery's OQ-1 resume decision: a landed-push crash with NO `rereview_requested` for its cycle resumes at `S5a_RETRIGGER_REVIEW` to re-post; one WITH it resumes at `S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW`). The `round_counter` ticks only when the subsequent poll attributes the re-review to our pushed SHA (the relocated INV-001 increment) — a timed-out re-trigger does NOT advance the counter.
96	- **Wave 6b (L3 only — decline fallback, FR-9/FR-10):** load `refs/auggie-fallback.md`. When the classifier returns `declined` (an Augment "abnormally large" decline observed at the initial S2 poll OR the S5 re-trigger poll), append a **`decline_detected`** run-log event, then engage the single-shot fallback: gate **strict-once** on the durable `auggie_review_invoked` idempotency record (comment-independent, survives resume — INV-R2; on engage, append an **`auggie_fallback_invoked{pr_number}`** event, the producer folded into that set), clamp the effective budget `effective_max_rounds := min(effective_max_rounds, 1)` (the `clamp_max_rounds` helper, recorded once via the **`max_rounds_clamped{effective_max_rounds}`** event — INV-R3 monotone-min fold), then invoke `> Skill sc:auggie-review-protocol --depth quick --remediation-offer --auggie-model claude-sonnet-4-6` and re-enter Waves 2-6 ONCE under the clamp (verify-before-remediate still applies — fallback findings are NOT trusted verbatim, FR-9.4). NO second invoke, NO second re-trigger, NO loop-back; `push_count <= max_rounds + 1` for the whole run. This is `sc:pr-submit` invoking its OWN review — do **NOT** "take the App's bait" by treating the App's `augment review` decline comment as our operator re-trigger. (`--depth quick` here targets `/sc:auggie-review` — a review, no `--fix` — so it does NOT conflict with the severity-routing STOP on `--depth quick --fix`.)
97	- **Wave 7:** load `refs/loop-guard.md`; the round counter ticks only at `S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW → S2_CLASSIFY`; HALT at `round_counter >= max_rounds`. Fallback outcomes REUSE the existing `terminal_clean` / `terminal_max_rounds` status values (OQ-2 reuse recommendation).
98	
99	## VAL — the §10 validation gate list (owned by the SKILL, not the core)
100	
101	Run IN ORDER, all green ⇒ `validation_status == "validated"` (the INV-016 predicate 2). Any
102	non-zero gate blocks the push:
103	
104	1. **VG-1** targeted tests (`uv run pytest <changed-area>`).
105	2. **VG-2** cross-cutting change → escalate to `make test`.
106	3. **VG-3** `make lint` (ruff check ONLY).
107	4. **VG-4** `uv run ruff format --check src/ tests/` (a SEPARATE gate — green VG-3 does NOT imply green VG-4; never collapse the two).
108	5. **VG-5** `make verify-sync` (skill-self-edits only; blocks at commit).
109	6. **VG-6** PR-target check (blocks at arm; the returned URL's `owner/repo` must equal the resolved origin repo).
110	
111	A validation retry does NOT increment `round_counter`.

113	## Will Do
114	
115	- Open the PR on the resolved origin repo with `--repo "$REPO"` pinned on every `gh` call (computed from origin, never bare).
116	- Verify before remediate; dispatch only verified findings; report unverified ones.
117	- Apply edits, validate, push, reply, and resolve ONLY within the ordinal ceiling.
118	- Keep the deterministic decisions in `superclaude.pr_submit`; keep `gh`/`git` I/O in the scripts.

121	
122	- Run headless / detached, or imply a background daemon (V1 limitation).
123	- Push to an upstream parent remote or to the repo's default/protected branch; open a PR against an upstream parent the CLI might default to.
124	- Auto-lock `detection-contract.md` or hard-guess the Augment bot login.
125	- Emit `--depth quick --fix` to troubleshoot (a STOP conflict).
126	- Apply any edit at L1, or push/reply at L2.

129	## Error Handling
130	
131	| Scenario | Behavior |
132	|----------|----------|
133	| `detection-contract.md` `locked:false` | HALT at arm with "probe first" (T-210). |
134	| Wrong origin / behind base branch / wrong-owner URL | HALT; instruct operator to close the misrouted PR (FM-11). |
135	| Review never arrives | `terminal_timeout`; no edits/push. |
136	| 403 / 429 / secondary-limit | exponential backoff 30→…→cap 300s, counts toward timeout. |
137	| `needs_human_decision` finding | `terminal_halted`; no auto-mutation (override, FR-4.4). |
138	| Validation failure | no push/reply/resolve; L2 halt; L3 one retry within budget. |

159	def evaluate_push_decision(
160	    *,
161	    monitor_ordinal: int,
162	    validation_status: str,
163	    needs_human_decision: bool,
164	    round_counter: int,
165	    max_rounds: int,
166	    applied_edits: int,
167	) -> PushDecision:
168	    """Evaluate the INV-016 5-predicate G-push conjunction (spec §5.3, verbatim).
169	
170	    A push is authorized iff ALL five predicates hold, ANDed immediately before the
171	    push: (1) ``monitor_ordinal >= 3``; (2) ``validation_status == "validated"``;
172	    (3) ``needs_human_decision == false`` for every finding; (4)
173	    ``round_counter < max_rounds``; (5) ``applied_edits > 0``. The returned
174	    :class:`PushDecision` records each predicate independently (the write-ahead
175	    audit primitive) so callers can assert the exact gate that blocked.
176	    """
177	    p1 = monitor_ordinal >= 3
178	    p2 = validation_status == "validated"
179	    p3 = not needs_human_decision
180	    p4 = round_counter < max_rounds
181	    p5 = applied_edits  # int; truthy when > 0
182	    authorized = bool(p1 and p2 and p3 and p4 and p5 > 0)
183	    return PushDecision(
184	        predicate_1_ordinal=p1,
185	        predicate_2_validated=p2,
186	        predicate_3_no_human=p3,
187	        predicate_4_under_cap=p4,
188	        predicate_5_applied_edits=p5,
189	        authorized=authorized,
190	    )

193	def push_fail_state(decision: PushDecision) -> MonitorState:
194	    """Map a blocked :class:`PushDecision` to its fail-route terminal (§5.3).
195	
196	    predicate 3 → HALT_HUMAN; 4 → HALT_MAX_ROUNDS; 5 → TERMINAL_CLEAN (report);
197	    1–2 → REPORT_ONLY. Evaluated in spec order so the most-specific HALT wins.
198	    """
199	    if not decision.predicate_3_no_human:
200	        return MonitorState.HALT_HUMAN
201	    if not decision.predicate_4_under_cap:
202	        return MonitorState.HALT_MAX_ROUNDS
203	    if decision.predicate_5_applied_edits <= 0:
204	        return MonitorState.TERMINAL_CLEAN
205	    return MonitorState.REPORT_ONLY

213	def push_idempotency_key(
214	    run_id: str, cycle_id: str, pre_push_sha: str, target_branch: str
215	) -> str:
216	    """The PRE-push idempotency key: ``push:<run_id>:<cycle_id>:<pre_push_sha>:<target_branch>``.
217	
218	    Keyed on the PRE-push SHA (not a post-hoc value) so a crash-window resume can
219	    match a ``push_initiated`` to its cycle and avoid a double push (INV-007).
220	    """
221	    return f"push:{run_id}:{cycle_id}:{pre_push_sha}:{target_branch}"

223	
224	def build_push_triad(
225	    *,
226	    run_id: str,
227	    cycle_id: str,
228	    round_counter: int,
229	    pre_push_sha: str,
230	    target_sha: str,
231	    target_branch: str,
232	    target_remote: str,
233	    decision: PushDecision,
234	) -> list[dict]:
235	    """Build the ordered write-ahead push triad records (spec §12.1, verbatim order).
236	
237	    Returns three event payloads IN ORDER — ``push_decision`` (the authorization
238	    audit, fsynced first), ``push_initiated`` (fsynced BEFORE the actual push), and
239	    ``push_completed`` (fsynced after). ``fsm.py`` only RECORDS these decisions; the
240	    actual push side-effect (the version-control push of ``<sha>:<branch>`` to the
241	    remote) is the SKILL's job. The idempotency key is on every record so recovery
242	    can match the triad.
243	    """
244	    key = push_idempotency_key(run_id, cycle_id, pre_push_sha, target_branch)
245	    common = {
246	        "run_id": run_id,
247	        "cycle_id": cycle_id,
248	        "idempotency_key": key,
249	        "pre_push_sha": pre_push_sha,
250	        "target_sha": target_sha,
251	        "target_branch": target_branch,
252	        "target_remote": target_remote,
253	    }
254	    return [
255	        {
256	            "event_type": "push_decision",
257	            "round_counter": round_counter,
258	            "authorized": decision.authorized,
259	            "predicates": {
260	                "p1_ordinal": decision.predicate_1_ordinal,
261	                "p2_validated": decision.predicate_2_validated,
262	                "p3_no_human": decision.predicate_3_no_human,
263	                "p4_under_cap": decision.predicate_4_under_cap,
264	                "p5_applied_edits": decision.predicate_5_applied_edits,
265	            },
266	            **common,
267	        },
268	        {
269	            "event_type": "push_initiated",
270	            "remote_ref": f"{target_remote}/{target_branch}",
271	            **common,
272	        },
273	        {"event_type": "push_completed", **common},
274	    ]

321	def build_reply(
322	    *,
323	    applied_edits: int,
324	    sha: str | None = None,
325	    hunk: str | None = None,
326	    trivial: bool = False,
327	) -> str:
328	    """Construct the thread-reply text citing `applied_edits` status (FR-6.1 / FR-6.5).
329	
330	    An ``applied_edits == 0`` cycle MUST say "no code change applied" and NEVER
331	    "resolved" (T-603), and NEVER embeds a suggestion block. A cycle that applied a
332	    grounded edit summarizes fix + SHA + passing validation; a TRIVIAL fix
333	    (``trivial`` and a ``hunk``) embeds a fenced ``suggestion`` block reproducing the
334	    applied hunk (T-640); a non-trivial fix carries prose + SHA only (T-641).
335	    """
336	    if applied_edits == 0:

339	            "reporting only, the thread is not marked resolved."

343	    ]

346	    if trivial and hunk:
347	        lines.append("```suggestion")
348	        lines.append(hunk)
349	        lines.append("```")

389	class DispatchPlan:
390	    """The plan for dispatching verified findings within the round budget (FR-3.4)."""
391	
392	    batches: list[list[Finding]] = field(default_factory=list)
393	    truncated: bool = False
394	    summary: str = ""

396	
397	def plan_dispatch(
398	    findings: list[Finding], *, max_rounds: int, current_round: int
399	) -> DispatchPlan:
400	    """Batch verified findings by file and TRUNCATE to the remaining round budget (FR-3.4).
401	
402	    Only dispatchable (non report-only) findings are batched. If the number of
403	    file-batches exceeds the remaining budget (``max_rounds - current_round``), the
404	    plan is truncated and ``truncated`` is set with a HALT summary (T-331).
405	    """
406	    dispatchable = [f for f in findings if route(f) != ROUTE_REPORT_ONLY]
407	    all_batches = batch_by_file(dispatchable)
408	    remaining = max(0, max_rounds - current_round)
409	    if len(all_batches) > remaining:
410	        kept = all_batches[:remaining]
411	        dropped = len(all_batches) - remaining
412	        return DispatchPlan(
413	            batches=kept,
414	            truncated=True,
415	            summary=(
416	                f"round budget exhausted: {dropped} finding-batch(es) deferred "
417	                f"(max_rounds={max_rounds}); HALT with residual summary"
418	            ),
419	        )
420	    return DispatchPlan(batches=all_batches, truncated=False)

426	
427	# The ordered gate list (spec §10). VG-3 (lint) and VG-4 (format) are TWO DISTINCT
428	# gates — the documented "make lint != CI ruff format" gotcha. Collapsing them is
429	# the bug T-511 regresses.
430	VALIDATION_GATES = ("VG-1", "VG-2", "VG-3", "VG-4", "VG-5", "VG-6")
431	
432	# Gates that MUST be present and green for "validated" (the mandatory trio: targeted
433	# tests + lint + format). VG-2 (cross-cutting escalation), VG-5 (sync, skill-self-edits
434	# only), and VG-6 (PR-target, checked at arm) are conditional — present only when
435	# applicable, but if present they must be green too.
436	MANDATORY_GATES = ("VG-1", "VG-3", "VG-4")
437	
438	
439	def run_validation_gates(results: dict[str, bool]) -> str:
440	    """Compute ``validation_status`` from the §10 gate results (the S7_VALIDATING driver).
441	
442	    Returns ``"validated"`` ONLY when every gate that ran is green AND the mandatory
443	    trio (VG-1 targeted tests, VG-3 lint, VG-4 format) are all present and green —
444	    the single definition consumed by the INV-016 G-push predicate (2). Any non-zero
445	    gate (or a missing mandatory gate, i.e. partial-green) yields ``"failed"``.
446	
447	    NFR-6: this function consumes pass/fail RESULTS; the actual gate commands
448	    (`uv run pytest` / `make lint` / `uv run ruff format --check`) are executed by the
449	    SKILL's VAL validator, never here — the core stays free of shell tokens. The
450	    VG-3≠VG-4 split is load-bearing: a green VG-3 with a failing/absent VG-4 is
451	    ``"failed"`` (T-511 / T-522), so green lint alone can never authorize a push.
452	    """
453	    # Iterate in gate order so the first failure is deterministic.
454	    for gate in VALIDATION_GATES:
455	        if gate in results and not results[gate]:
456	            return "failed"
457	    for gate in MANDATORY_GATES:
458	        if not results.get(gate):
459	            return "failed"
460	    return "validated"

463	def pr_target_ok(pr_url: str, target_repo: str) -> bool:
464	    """Whether ``pr_url`` targets ``target_repo`` — the VG-6 / FM-11 misroute check.
465	
466	    ``target_repo`` is the RESOLVED ``owner/repo`` of the origin remote, NOT a
467	    hardcoded constant: the SKILL resolves it at runtime (origin's ``nameWithOwner``,
468	    fallback the origin remote URL) and passes it in. A returned URL whose owner/repo is
469	    NOT ``target_repo`` (e.g. the host CLI silently defaulted the PR onto the upstream
470	    PARENT of a fork) is a misroute → the caller HALTs (`terminal_failed`) and instructs
471	    the operator to close it (T-108 / FM-11). Core-pure: a pure string check, no
472	    version-control command tokens.
473	    """
474	    if not pr_url or not target_repo:
475	        return False
476	    return f"/{target_repo}/" in pr_url or pr_url.rstrip("/").endswith(target_repo)
477

479	def origin_ok(origin_url: str, target_repo: str) -> bool:
480	    """Whether the `origin` remote URL matches the resolved ``target_repo`` (pre-PR check, T-106).
481	
482	    ``target_repo`` is the resolved ``owner/repo`` the PR is meant to land on (the
483	    SKILL resolves it from origin at runtime, never a module constant). Accepts https
484	    and ssh remote URLs, with or without a trailing ``.``-prefixed VCS suffix. The repo
485	    is the URL's TRAILING component, so the match is BOUNDARY-anchored — ``owner`` must
486	    follow a ``/`` (https / ssh-url form) or ``:`` (scp-style ``user@host:owner/repo``)
487	    separator, and ``repo`` must be followed by end-of-string or a ``.``-prefixed suffix
488	    — NOT a bare substring. A bare substring would falsely pass ``acme/widgets`` against
489	    an origin of ``acme/widgets-upstream``; the boundary anchor rejects it. A mismatch
490	    (origin points somewhere other than the intended target) → HALT before opening the
491	    PR. Core-pure: a pure string check (the SKILL runs the actual remote query and
492	    passes its result here).
493	    """
494	    if not origin_url or not target_repo:
495	        return False
496	    stripped = origin_url.rstrip("/")
497	    if stripped == target_repo:
498	        return True
499	    for sep in ("/", ":"):
500	        marker = sep + target_repo
501	        idx = stripped.rfind(marker)
502	        if idx == -1:
503	            continue
504	        rest = stripped[idx + len(marker) :]
505	        if rest == "" or rest.startswith("."):
506	            return True
507	    return False

512	
513	    Pure arithmetic: ``commits_behind`` is computed by the SKILL against the repo's
514	    ACTUAL default branch (resolved by the SKILL from the repo's ``defaultBranchRef``, or

520	def is_cross_cutting(changed_files: list[str]) -> bool:
521	    """Whether a change is cross-cutting → escalate VG-1 targeted tests to VG-2 `make test`.
522	
523	    Cross-cutting when ≥5 files, OR ≥2 distinct top-level packages under ``src/``, OR
524	    shared infra is touched (hooks / pyproject / conftest / run-log / fsm). A single
525	    file in one area is targeted-only (T-501); a broad change escalates (T-502).
526	    The actual ``make test`` execution is the SKILL's job (NFR-6).
527	    """
528	    if len(changed_files) >= 5:
529	        return True
530	    shared_markers = ("hooks/", "pyproject", "conftest", "run_log", "fsm.py")
531	    if any(marker in f for f in changed_files for marker in shared_markers):
532	        return True
533	    packages: set[str] = set()
534	    for f in changed_files:
535	        parts = f.split("/")
536	        # top-level package under src/superclaude/<pkg>/... or src/<pkg>/...
537	        if "superclaude" in parts:
538	            idx = parts.index("superclaude")
539	            if idx + 1 < len(parts):
540	                packages.add(parts[idx + 1])
541	        elif len(parts) >= 2:
542	            packages.add(
543	                parts[0]
544	                if parts[0] != "src"
545	                else parts[1]
546	                if len(parts) > 1
547	                else parts[0]
548	            )
549	    return len(packages) >= 2

553	# Poll timing: backoff + timeout arithmetic (FR-2.3 / FR-2.5 / NFR-2)

557	BACKOFF_BASE = MIN_POLL_INTERVAL  # 30s
558	BACKOFF_CAP = 300  # 5 min

560	
561	def next_backoff(prev_interval: int) -> int:
562	    """Next exponential backoff interval: ``30 → 60 → 120 → … → cap 300`` (FR-2.5).
563	
564	    ``prev_interval <= 0`` (or below base) restarts at the 30s base; otherwise it
565	    doubles, capped at 300s. A successful poll resets the caller's interval to 0 so
566	    the next backoff restarts at the base (T-231: backoff 30, 60, reset).
567	    """
568	    if prev_interval < BACKOFF_BASE:
569	        return BACKOFF_BASE
570	    return min(prev_interval * 2, BACKOFF_CAP)

578	def poll_outcome(review_state: str, elapsed_seconds: int, timeout: int) -> MonitorState:
579	    """Map a poll result + elapsed time to the next FSM state.
580	
581	    A ``clean``/``findings`` review proceeds (S2_CLASSIFY); a still-``polling`` review
582	    that has exceeded the wall-clock timeout fires TERMINAL_TIMEOUT (T-221/T-222);
583	    otherwise polling continues (loop back to S2_CLASSIFY).
584	    """
585	    if review_state in ("clean", "findings"):
586	        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
587	    if timed_out(elapsed_seconds, timeout):
588	        return MonitorState.TERMINAL_TIMEOUT
589	    return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY

592	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
593	# transition() — the transition table (spec §5.4: a table, not nested ifs)
594	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
595	
596	
597	def transition(
598	    state: MonitorState, event: str, context: dict | None = None
599	) -> MonitorState:
600	    """Return the next state for ``(state, event)`` under the ordinal ceiling.
601	
602	    The ``needs_human_decision`` override is evaluated FIRST (pre-gate, §5.2): any
603	    event in a cycle carrying ``needs_human_decision`` routes to HALT_HUMAN
604	    regardless of ordinal. Otherwise the edge is looked up in the transition table,
605	    with the three ordinal gates applied at their edges.
606	    """
607	    ctx = context or {}
608	    ordinal = int(ctx.get("monitor_ordinal", 0))
609	
610	    # Pre-gate override (the ONLY ceiling short-circuit).
611	    if ctx.get("needs_human_decision"):
612	        return MonitorState.HALT_HUMAN
613	
614	    edge = (state, event)
615	
616	    if edge == (MonitorState.S0_IDLE, "arm"):
617	        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY if gate_arm(ordinal) else MonitorState.S0_IDLE
618	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY, "no_review"):
619	        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY  # loop back (poll again)
620	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY, "clean"):
621	        return MonitorState.TERMINAL_CLEAN
622	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY, "findings"):
623	        # round-budget gate evaluated here
624	        if should_halt_rounds(
625	            int(ctx.get("round_counter", 0)),
626	            int(ctx.get("max_rounds", DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS)),
627	        ):
628	            return MonitorState.HALT_MAX_ROUNDS
629	        return MonitorState.S2B_VERIFY
630	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2B_VERIFY, "verified"):
631	        return MonitorState.S3_DIAGNOSE
632	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2B_VERIFY, "unverified"):
633	        return MonitorState.REPORT_ONLY  # no round consumed
634	    if edge == (MonitorState.S3_DIAGNOSE, "diagnosed"):
635	        # G-edit: ordinal >= 2 enters S3_FIXING; else PROPOSED (offer, no edits)
636	        return MonitorState.S3_FIXING if gate_edit(ordinal) else MonitorState.PROPOSED
637	    if edge == (MonitorState.S3_FIXING, "edits_applied"):
638	        return MonitorState.S7_VALIDATING
639	    if edge == (MonitorState.S7_VALIDATING, "validated"):
640	        # G-push handled by evaluate_push_decision at the caller; default edge
641	        return MonitorState.S4_PUSHING
642	    if edge == (MonitorState.S7_VALIDATING, "validation_failed"):
643	        return MonitorState.VALIDATION_FAIL
644	    if edge == (MonitorState.S4_PUSHING, "pushed"):
645	        return MonitorState.S6_REPLYING
646	    if edge == (MonitorState.S6_REPLYING, "replied"):
647	        return MonitorState.RESOLVING
648	    if edge == (MonitorState.RESOLVING, "resolved"):
649	        # V1.1 (FR-8.1): after resolve, route to S5a to post the re-trigger comment
650	        # BEFORE awaiting the re-review (a push does NOT auto-trigger an Augment
651	        # re-review). The increment is NOT here; INV-001's edge is below.
652	        return MonitorState.S5A_RETRIGGER_REVIEW
653	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5A_RETRIGGER_REVIEW, "retriggered"):
654	        # The re-trigger comment was posted → await the re-review (INV-R1). The
655	        # re-trigger itself does NOT tick round_counter.
656	        return MonitorState.S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW
657	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW, "rereview_attributed"):
658	        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY  # loop-guard increments at this edge (INV-001)
659	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW, "timeout"):
660	        return MonitorState.TERMINAL_TIMEOUT
661	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW, "declined"):
662	        # V1.1 (FR-9): a decline observed at the S5 re-trigger poll → oversized-PR
663	        # auggie-review fallback (S5b). Sibling of rereview_attributed/timeout; the
664	        # INV-001 edge above is unchanged.
665	        return MonitorState.S5B_AUGGIE_FALLBACK
666	    if edge == (MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY, "declined"):
667	        # V1.1 (FR-9.1): a decline observed at the INITIAL S2 poll → fallback (S5b).
668	        return MonitorState.S5B_AUGGIE_FALLBACK
669	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5B_AUGGIE_FALLBACK, "fallback_findings"):
670	        # The fallback /sc:auggie-review produced findings → re-enter classification
671	        # ONCE under the clamp (no loop-back).
672	        return MonitorState.S2_CLASSIFY
673	    if edge == (MonitorState.S5B_AUGGIE_FALLBACK, "fallback_skip"):
674	        # Single-shot fallback terminal selector (FR-10, OQ-2 reuse): clean residual →
675	        # TERMINAL_CLEAN; residual findings remain → HALT_MAX_ROUNDS.
676	        return (
677	            MonitorState.HALT_MAX_ROUNDS
678	            if ctx.get("fallback_residual_findings")
679	            else MonitorState.TERMINAL_CLEAN
680	        )
681	
682	    # Unknown edge: stay put (defensive; real runs never hit this).
683	    return state

1	"""The single finite state machine for ``sc:pr-submit`` (spec §5).
2	
3	Encodes the gate table as three one-line ordinal checks (G-arm / G-edit / G-push)
4	plus the ``needs_human_decision`` pre-gate override (§5.2), the INV-016 5-predicate
5	G-push conjunction (§5.3), and the ``run_skill(...)`` integration driver that the
6	spec's test bodies call and assert on (returns a :class:`~superclaude.pr_submit.models.SkillResult`).
7	
8	NFR-6 / AC-9 / FR-G1 core purity: this module imports NO ``anthropic`` SDK and
9	contains ZERO shell / version-control command tokens. All side-effecting I/O (the
10	review poll, the push, the reply/resolve, the validation commands) is performed by
11	the skill's bash scripts and the SKILL.md VAL validator; ``fsm.py`` consumes
12	already-fetched / already-classified data and records DECISIONS only. The
13	side-effect seams below default to recording-only callables.
14	
15	This module is extended by Phase 6 (the §10 validation-gate driver, ``S7_VALIDATING``)
16	and Phase 7 (the L3 push triad ``S4_PUSHING`` / ``S6_REPLYING`` / ``RESOLVING``).
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import argparse
22	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
23	from typing import Callable
24	
25	from .loop_guard import should_halt as loop_guard_should_halt
26	from .models import Finding, MonitorState, PushDecision, SkillResult
27	from .severity_router import ROUTE_REPORT_ONLY, remap_severity, route
28	
29	# Defaults (spec FR-1.1 / FR-2.3).
30	DEFAULT_MONITOR = 1
31	DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS = 2
32	HARD_CAP_MAX_ROUNDS = 5
33	MIN_POLL_INTERVAL = 30
34	DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 600
35	
36	POLL_INTERVAL_ERROR = "minimum is 30 seconds"
37	MAX_ROUNDS_ERROR = "--max-rounds hard cap is 5"
38	
39	# The exact L1 user-facing proposal prompt (FR-4.1 / T-402).
40	PROPOSE_PROMPT = "fix these? y/n"
41	
42	
43	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
44	# Argument parsing (spec FR-1.1 / FR-1.2 / FR-1.6 / FR-1.7)
45	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
46	
47	
48	@dataclass
49	class SkillArgs:
50	    """Parsed `sc:pr-submit` flags."""
51	
52	    monitor: int = DEFAULT_MONITOR
53	    max_rounds: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS
54	    poll_interval: int = MIN_POLL_INTERVAL
55	    timeout: int = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
56	    base: str | None = None
57	    head: str | None = None
58	    title: str | None = None
59	    body: str | None = None
60	    output_dir: str | None = None
61	    resume: str | None = None
62	    yes: bool = False
63	
64	    @property
65	    def armed(self) -> bool:
66	        """The monitor arms only at ordinal >= 1 (G-arm). L0 never arms (T-103/T-110)."""
67	        return self.monitor >= 1
68	
69	
70	def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
71	    """Build the argparse parser for the `sc:pr-submit` command surface."""
72	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="sc:pr-submit", add_help=False)
73	    parser.add_argument(
74	        "--monitor", type=int, choices=[0, 1, 2, 3], default=DEFAULT_MONITOR
75	    )
76	    parser.add_argument(
77	        "--max-rounds", dest="max_rounds", type=int, default=DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS
78	    )
79	    parser.add_argument(
80	        "--poll-interval", dest="poll_interval", type=int, default=MIN_POLL_INTERVAL
81	    )
82	    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
83	    parser.add_argument("--base", default=None)
84	    parser.add_argument("--head", default=None)
85	    parser.add_argument("--title", default=None)
86	    parser.add_argument("--body", default=None)
87	    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", dest="output_dir", default=None)
88	    parser.add_argument("--resume", default=None)
89	    parser.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true")
90	    return parser
91	
92	
93	def parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> SkillArgs:
94	    """Parse `argv` into :class:`SkillArgs`, enforcing the documented bounds.
95	
96	    Raises :class:`ValueError` with the EXACT spec message when ``--poll-interval``
97	    is below 30 (T-111: "minimum is 30 seconds") or ``--max-rounds`` exceeds the
98	    hard cap of 5 (T-102). ``--monitor`` choices are enforced by argparse (T-101).
99	    """
100	    parser = build_arg_parser()
101	    ns = parser.parse_args(argv)
102	    if ns.poll_interval < MIN_POLL_INTERVAL:
103	        raise ValueError(f"--poll-interval {POLL_INTERVAL_ERROR}")
104	    if ns.max_rounds > HARD_CAP_MAX_ROUNDS:
105	        raise ValueError(MAX_ROUNDS_ERROR)
106	    if ns.max_rounds < 0:
107	        raise ValueError("--max-rounds must be >= 0")
108	    return SkillArgs(
109	        monitor=ns.monitor,
110	        max_rounds=ns.max_rounds,
111	        poll_interval=ns.poll_interval,
112	        timeout=ns.timeout,
113	        base=ns.base,
114	        head=ns.head,
115	        title=ns.title,
116	        body=ns.body,
117	        output_dir=ns.output_dir,
118	        resume=ns.resume,
119	        yes=ns.yes,
120	    )
121	
122	
123	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
124	# Gate predicates (spec §5.2 / §5.3) — one-line ordinal checks, never nested ifs
125	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
126	
127	
128	def gate_arm(ordinal: int) -> bool:
129	    """G-arm: ``ordinal >= 1`` to leave S0_IDLE and enter polling."""
130	    return ordinal >= 1

1	---
2	name: pr-submit
3	description: "Open a PR on the fork and arm an in-session PR-review auto-remediation monitor — poll for the Augment review, re-grade + verify findings, dispatch verified ones to /sc:troubleshoot, then (at higher --monitor ordinals) fix, validate, push, reply, and resolve under a capped monotonic round counter."
4	category: quality
5	complexity: advanced
6	mcp-servers: [sequential, serena, auggie]
7	personas: [analyzer, architect, security, qa, devops]
8	argument-hint: "--monitor {0,1,2,3} [--max-rounds N≤5] [--poll-interval ≥30] [--timeout 600] [--base <branch>] [--head <branch>] [--title ...] [--body ...] [--output-dir <dir>] [--resume <run-log.jsonl>]"
9	version: "1.0"
10	---
11	
12	# /sc:pr-submit - PR Review Auto-Remediation Monitor
13	
14	## Triggers
15	
16	Explicit only — three activation paths:
17	
18	1. **Direct:** the user runs `/sc:pr-submit --monitor {0,1,2,3}` to open a PR (and optionally arm the monitor).
19	2. **PR-creation hook:** after a successful `gh pr create`, the `offer-pr-review.sh` hook mentions `sc:pr-submit --monitor` alongside `/sc:auggie-review` (the hook NEVER arms a monitor itself, NEVER implies level-3 without explicit invocation).
20	3. **Programmatic:** another skill invokes the protocol via the Skill tool.
21	
22	## Required Input
23	
24	| Input | Required | Notes |
25	|-------|----------|-------|
26	| `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` | No (default 1) | The autonomy ceiling on a single FSM. Explicit 0 = open PR only (byte-identical to today). |
27	| PR context (`--head`/`--base`/`--title`/`--body`) OR an existing PR number | Yes | To open or attach to the PR. |
28	
29	**STOP** if `--monitor >= 1` and the PR cannot be confirmed on the resolved target repo (origin's `owner/repo`, via `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`), or if `detection-contract.md` is `locked: false` (run the R1 probe first — T-210).
30	
31	## Usage
32	
33	```text
34	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 0 --head feature/x --title "..." --body "..."     # open PR only (zero regression)
35	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 1 --head feature/x                                 # arm + poll + propose (no edits)
36	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 2 --head feature/x                                 # + fix locally, HALT before push
37	/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --max-rounds 3 --head feature/x                  # full loop: fix→push→reply→resolve
38	/sc:pr-submit --resume <repo-root>/.dev/pr-monitor/pr-42-.../monitor-run-42.jsonl
39	```
40	
41	## Options
42	
43	| Flag | Default | Description |
44	|------|---------|-------------|
45	| `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` | 1 | Capability ceiling (G-arm/G-edit/G-push gates). |
46	| `--max-rounds N` | 2 | Remediation cycles; hard cap 5 (reject >5). |
47	| `--poll-interval S` | 30 | Poll interval; minimum 30 seconds (reject <30). |
48	| `--timeout S` | 600 | Review-wait wall-clock timeout (~10 min). |
49	| `--base <branch>` | repo default branch | PR base branch; defaults to the repo's actual default (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`), overridable here. |
50	| `--head <branch>` | — | PR head branch. |
51	| `--title` / `--body` | — | PR title / body. |
52	| `--output-dir <dir>` | `.dev/pr-monitor/pr-<N>-<ts>/` | Run-log + artifacts dir. |
53	| `--resume <jsonl>` | — | Reconstruct state from a write-ahead run-log. |
54	
55	## Behavioral Flow
56	
57	This command does ONLY parse + environment-validate + handoff. It parses the flags, verifies the PR target is the resolved origin repo (origin's `owner/repo`, never an upstream parent the host's CLI might default to), and hands off to the protocol skill via the Activation section below. The full behavioral specification — the FSM, the detection contract, severity routing, verify-before-remediate, troubleshoot dispatch, validation gates, the push triad, reply/resolve, and the loop guard — lives in the skill.
58	
59	## Arming (R1 detection probe, T-210)
60	
61	`--monitor 0` always works (it just opens the PR). To arm at `--monitor >= 1`, the detection contract must be locked. The shipped `refs/detection-contract.md` ships `locked: false`, so a fresh clone safely HALTs ("probe first"). To arm on a given repo, run the R1 probe once against a PR the Augment App has reviewed (capture `augment_bot_login`, `emission_shape`, `findings_locus`, etc.), write the gitignored operator-local override `<repo-root>/.dev/pr-monitor/detection-contract.locked.md` with `locked: true`, and the arm path (`DetectionContract.for_arming()`) prefers it (resolved relative to the cwd). The repo-specific bot identity therefore never ships in the distributable skill.
62	
63	## Activation
64	
65	**MANDATORY**: Before executing any protocol steps, invoke:
66	> Skill sc:pr-submit-protocol
67	
68	Pass the following context:
69

16	## Purpose
17	
18	`sc:pr-submit` opens a PR on the resolved origin repo (origin's `owner/repo` — never an upstream parent), arms an
19	**in-session** Monitor that polls for the Augment Code review, re-grades each finding's severity
20	through the reused auggie-review rubric, **verifies each finding grounds in real code before
21	remediating** (verify-before-remediate — no round and no push is ever spent on a hallucinated or
22	stale finding), dispatches only verified findings to `/sc:troubleshoot` for diagnosis, then — at
23	higher autonomy ordinals — applies the fix itself, validates, pushes, replies on the finding
24	thread, and resolves it. It terminates deterministically under a capped, monotonic round counter.
25	
26	**The `--monitor {0,1,2,3}` ordinal is a capability ceiling on a SINGLE finite state machine**
27	(`refs/state-machine.md`), compared at exactly three gates plus one override — NOT four divergent
28	code paths. The deterministic decisions (classification, severity remap, the FSM gate table, the
29	loop-guard fence-post, the push conjunction) are owned by the importable `superclaude.pr_submit`
30	Python core; this SKILL.md owns sequencing, the Monitor arming, the `gh`/`git` I/O (via the bash
31	scripts), and the §10 VAL validator.
32	
33	> **Honest framing (FR-2.4, NOT a daemon).** The Monitor is **in-session**: closing the session
34	> loses the monitor. Durability comes from the write-ahead JSONL run-log + `--resume`, never from
35	> detachment. This skill cannot survive its own session. Do NOT imply a background daemon.
36	>
37	> **Top-level activation required.** This skill MUST run in the main orchestrating session (so it
38	> has the `Monitor` tool and can `> Skill sc:troubleshoot-protocol`). Do NOT run it inside an
39	> Agent-tool subagent that itself spawns skills.

75	## Wave / Phase Structure (refs are LAZY-loaded per wave, never pre-loaded)
76	
77	```text
78	Wave 0: Open PR + verify target   ← (no ref; gh pr create --repo, pre-PR checks)
79	Wave 1: Arm + poll                ← loads refs/detection-contract.md (arm gate) + refs/augment-poll.md
80	Wave 2: Classify + re-grade       ← loads refs/severity-routing.md
81	Wave 3: Verify-before-remediate   ← loads refs/finding-verify.md
82	Wave 4: Diagnose + (L2+) fix      ← loads refs/troubleshoot-dispatch.md
83	Wave 5: Validate                  ← the VAL validator (§10 gate list, below)
84	Wave 6: (L3) push + reply + resolve + re-trigger ← loads refs/thread-reply.md + refs/review-retrigger.md (S5a)
85	Wave 6b: (L3) decline → auggie fallback           ← loads refs/auggie-fallback.md (S5b, strict-once)

Only L3 proceeds to Wave 6.
95	- **Wave 6 (L3 only):** load `refs/thread-reply.md`. The deterministic core DECIDES (evaluates the INV-016 conjunction, records the write-ahead push triad `push_decision` → `push_initiated` (fsynced BEFORE the push) → `push_completed`, keyed on the PRE-push idempotency key `push:<run_id>:<cycle_id>:<pre_push_sha>:<target_branch>`); the SKILL performs the actual `git push origin <target_sha>:<target_branch>` (never an upstream parent remote, never the repo's default/protected branch) ONLY when the conjunction holds, then reply (citing `applied_edits` status — `applied_edits==0` says "no code change applied", never "resolved") and resolve via `scripts/reply-resolve-thread.sh` (reply FIRST, then resolve). **S5a re-trigger (FR-8):** load `refs/review-retrigger.md`; a push does NOT auto-trigger an Augment re-review — AFTER resolve, and ONLY when this cycle applied edits (`applied_edits > 0`), post the re-trigger comment via `scripts/retrigger-review.sh --pr <N>` BEFORE re-entering the S5 poll. The core decides whether/when to re-trigger (`do_retrigger` seam, INV-R1: at most once per push cycle, `rereview_request_count <= max_rounds`); the script does the `gh api` issue-comment POST (NFR-6). The `round_counter` ticks only when the subsequent poll attributes the re-review to our pushed SHA (the relocated INV-001 increment) — a timed-out re-trigger does NOT advance the counter.
96	- **Wave 6b (L3 only — decline fallback, FR-9/FR-10):** load `refs/auggie-fallback.md`. NO second invoke, NO second re-trigger, NO loop-back; `push_count <= max_rounds + 1` for the whole run. This is `sc:pr-submit` invoking its OWN review — do **NOT** "take the App's bait" by treating the App's `augment review` decline comment as our operator re-trigger. 97	- **Wave 7:** load `refs/loop-guard.md`; the round counter ticks only at `S5_AWAITING_REREVIEW → S2_CLASSIFY`; HALT at `round_counter >= max_rounds`. Fallback outcomes REUSE the existing `terminal_clean` / `terminal_max_rounds` status values (OQ-2 reuse recommendation).
98	
99	## VAL — the §10 validation gate list (owned by the SKILL, not the core)
100	
101	Run IN ORDER, all green ⇒ `validation_status == "validated"` (the INV-016 predicate 2). Any
102	non-zero gate blocks the push:
103	
104	1. **VG-1** targeted tests (`uv run pytest <changed-area>`).

118	- Keep the deterministic decisions in `superclaude.pr_submit`; keep `gh`/`git` I/O in the scripts.

120	## Will Not Do
121	
122	- Run headless / detached, or imply a background daemon (V1 limitation).
123	- Push to an upstream parent remote or to the repo's default/protected branch; open a PR against an upstream parent the CLI might default to.

126	- Apply any edit at L1, or push/reply at L2.

129	## Error Handling
130	
131	| Scenario | Behavior |
132	|----------|----------|
133	| `detection-contract.md` `locked:false` | HALT at arm with "probe first" (T-210). |
134	| Wrong origin / behind base branch / wrong-owner URL | HALT; instruct operator to close the misrouted PR (FM-11). |
135	| Review never arrives | `terminal_timeout`; no edits/push. |
136	| 403 / 429 / secondary-limit | exponential backoff 30→…→cap 300s, counts toward timeout. |
137	| `needs_human_decision` finding | `terminal_halted`; no auto-mutation (override, FR-4.4). |
138	| Validation failure | no push/reply/resolve; L2 halt; L3 one retry within budget. |
139	| Crash mid-push | `--resume` 3-way recovery (§12); no double push, no re-fix. |

1	# Augment Poll (C2) — the poller contract
2	
3	This ref pins the poll surface and timing for the in-session Monitor. The poll **script**
4	(`scripts/poll-augment-review.sh`) performs a single `gh`/`gh api` poll and emits one JSON line; the
5	**FSM** (`superclaude.pr_submit`) does the backoff arithmetic. This split keeps `gh` out of the
6	deterministic core (NFR-6) — the script touches `gh`, the core decides.
7	
8	> Every `gh`/`gh api` call below pins the RESOLVED `--repo <owner/repo>` (origin's `nameWithOwner`,
9	> FR-1.3 / AC-7). A bare `gh` without `--repo` is a defect (T-104 greps for it).
10	
11	## Poll surfaces (FR-2.1)
12	
13	Primary, the exact `--json` field set from the spec:
14	
15	```bash
16	gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json number,url,headRefName,headRefOid,baseRefName,reviews,comments
17	```
18	
19	- `headRefOid` = the head SHA (used by INV-001 `sha_attributed_to_our_push` and the inline-reply
20	  `commit_id`).
21	- `reviews` = `{author{login}, authorAssociation, state, body, submittedAt, url}`.
22	- `comments` = PR conversation comments (NOT inline review comments).
23	
24	REST surfaces (inline-comment ids / `in_reply_to_id` are not on `gh pr view`, so REST is required):
25	
26	```bash
27	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/reviews
28	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/pulls/<N>/comments
29	gh api repos/<owner/repo>/commits/<headSHA>/check-runs   # only if the probe shows emission_shape==check_run
30	```
31	
32	Classification is pure against the probe-locked `DetectionContract` (`detection-contract.md`): key on
33	`augment_bot_login`; four states no-review / clean / findings / **declined** (T-201/202/203 + FR-9.1).
34	The V1.1 `declined` state fires when an Augment-authored comment matches BOTH probe-locked decline
35	regexes (`decline_phrase_regex` "abnormally large" AND `decline_retrigger_regex` "comment
36	augment/auggie/augmentcode review"), watermark-aware (a stale pre-watermark decline is ignored, EC-23).
37	The decline ARITHMETIC (the both-regex AND, the watermark comparison, the strict-once routing) stays in
38	the deterministic core; only the decline raw-surfacing comes from this poll script — the same
39	script-polls / FSM-decides seam as the other states. The decline is posted by the App as a **PR
40	conversation comment** (the `gh pr view --json comments` surface, equivalently `issues/<N>/comments` —
41	the same surface `retrigger-review.sh` posts to), NOT as an inline review comment. The poll script
42	therefore **merges** the conversation comments (`.comments` from `gh pr view`) with the inline review
43	comments (`pulls/<N>/comments`) into the emitted `comments` array, so the classifier sees the decline;
44	surfacing only the inline comments would make `declined` unreachable in production. (The classifier's
45	finding-comment rule requires `path`+`line`, so the path-less conversation comments are never miscounted
46	as findings.)
47	
48	## Interval, timeout, backoff (FR-2.3 / FR-2.5 / NFR-2)
49	
50	- **Interval ≥ 30s.** A value below 30 is **rejected, not rounded** ("minimum is 30 seconds", T-111).
51	- **Timeout default 600s** (~10 min), configurable; **wall-clock since entering wait** (T-221/T-222).
52	- **Exponential backoff on 403 / 429 / secondary-limit:** `30 → 60 → 120 → … → cap 300s`, resetting
53	  on a successful poll (T-231). The backoff **counts toward the wall-clock timeout**.
54	
55	## Division of labour (the NFR-6 seam)
56	
57	- The **poll script** does ONE `gh`/`gh api` poll and returns a status line (`polling` / `clean` /
58	  `findings`, plus the raw payload for classification). It performs no arithmetic and holds no state.
59	- The **FSM** owns the backoff arithmetic (which interval to use next, whether the cap or the timeout
60	  is reached) and the state transitions. This keeps the `gh` I/O isolated to the script and the
61	  deterministic decisions in `superclaude.pr_submit` (NFR-6). The ref explicitly assigns the backoff
62	  arithmetic to the FSM, never the script.
